scope: 42 of the 69 numbered assertions have complete checked proofs. The remaining 27, including the main theorem, have no complete proof here. Checked components and conditional implications do not count as complete proofs of their parent assertions. Lemma 2.2 is represented by its finite probability laws.

checked_component_catalog.description: A proper k-edge-coloring gives at most floor(|X|/2) edges of each color inside X, hence at most k*floor(|X|/2) induced edges. An overfull set prevents such a coloring.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The necessary direction only; no sufficient condition for edge-colorability is proved.

checked_component_catalog.description: Every proper k-edge-coloring of a finite simple graph has degree at most k at each vertex and maximum degree at most k.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This is a lower bound on the number of colors, not Vizing's upper bound.

checked_component_catalog.description: At every vertex of degree k each of the k colors occurs exactly once. In a k-regular simple graph each color subgraph is a perfect matching. Equality in the internal-edge count saturates every color class.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: These consequences require a supplied proper coloring. Boundary-color injectivity and the actual odd-clique contraction are proved in separate checked components.

checked_component_catalog.description: Integer deficiency, cut parity and odd-set threshold identities, with the incidence-counting identity supplied where needed.

checked_component_catalog.description: If f is even, d <= f and 2e <= d+1, then 2e <= f.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The numerical rounding implication. The actual incidence inequality and the completion odd-set proof are recorded separately under auxiliary_balanced_incidences and auxiliary_odd_sets.

checked_component_catalog.description: The nonnegative integer pairs with 0 < q+l and q+2l < 4 are exactly (1,0), (0,1), (2,0), (3,0) and (1,1).
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The input counting bound is assumed. No robust partition, critical-graph estimate or exclusion of a component case is proved.

checked_component_catalog.description: The order threshold n1 <= n' follows from 4*n1 <= n, n <= 4*Delta and Delta+1 <= n'.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Only the numerical threshold transfer; existence and properties of a critical subgraph are not proved.

checked_component_catalog.description: The supplied absorber parameter equations imply the selected-color total, reserved-degree identity, residual degree 2r and total k colors.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The parameter equalities and degree inequalities are hypotheses. Existence, disjointness, graph-degree identities and exhaustion of actual edges are not proved.

checked_component_catalog.description: For the actual graph on (Fin 4 x Fin Delta) + Fin 5, adjacency is symmetric and irreflexive; order is 4*Delta+5. For every Delta >= 3, the complete degree formulas, maximum degree Delta and connectedness are proved.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every Delta >= 3, the actual graph has degree sum 4*Delta*(Delta+1) and edgeFinset cardinality 2*Delta*(Delta+1).
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This component counts all edges of the actual graph. The bounds for every induced vertex set are proved separately in the family_no_overfull component.

checked_component_catalog.description: The actual Petersen multigraph with Delta-2 separate copies of each spoke has no proper Delta-edge-coloring for every Delta >= 3. Ordinary Petersen non-3-edge-colorability is a specialization.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This component concerns the complete weighted Petersen multigraph. Deleting one vertex and transferring the obstruction through the four expanded cliques are proved separately.

checked_component_catalog.description: The finite matching encodings give zero or four nonspoke edges in each perfect matching, and such patterns cannot cover all ten nonspoke edges exactly once.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This finite classification is used by the weighted Petersen obstruction. The actual expansion is handled in the family_coloring_obstruction component.

checked_component_catalog.description: For each of the 1024 ten-bit masks with odd vertex count, the explicit Petersen cut sum is at least three and the spoke-cut sum is at least one; the weighted cut expression is at least Delta for Delta >= 3.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: These are proofs of the finite mask cut inequalities. Their correspondence with arbitrary whole-clique subsets of the actual family is proved in the family_whole_clique_counting component.

checked_component_catalog.description: The clique cut inequality, odd-deficiency rounding, edge-count expression, whole-order threshold and degree-ratio gap satisfy the numerical identities used in Section 7.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Arithmetic components only; a numerical inequality involving a putative cut does not prove the graph cut has that value.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every real c < 1/4, sufficiently large parameters satisfy c <= Delta/(4*Delta+5), and arbitrarily large odd parameters >=3 satisfy this inequality.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This component proves the numerical quantifiers. The complete graph-existence statement is tracked separately as Corollary 7.2.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every finite simple graph and actual vertex set, internal-edge degree sums, internal-plus-boundary counting, deficiency identities, and the equivalence between odd-set overfullness and small deficiency are proved. A partially intersected clique contributes its actual crossing-edge lower bound.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: These are generic graph-counting theorems. They do not supply any robust partition or sufficient coloring condition for the main theorem.

checked_component_catalog.description: Actual clique edge counts imply saturation for an odd clique with as many colors as vertices. Each color misses exactly one vertex of any saturated odd set, so distinct edges crossing its boundary have distinct colors.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The color statements assume a supplied proper coloring and prove the consequences needed for contraction.

checked_component_catalog.description: A proper coloring of the weighted Petersen graph with outer vertex zero deleted would extend across the deleted vertex. Regularity, the remaining order, the exact remaining edge count, unique missing vertices, and properness of the restored coloring are proved for the actual edge copies. Thus deletion preserves the Delta-coloring obstruction.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The specialization proves the obstruction for the deleted weighted multigraph. The expansion into a simple graph is proved separately.

The correspondence of edge endpoints, injectivity of the lifted edges, and properness after contraction are proved.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This component proves the Delta-coloring obstruction for the actual family. The explicit Delta+1 coloring is a separate component.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every odd Delta >= 3, the actual sharpness graph admits an explicitly defined proper edge coloring with Delta+1 colors. The assignment is well-defined on unordered edges and injective on edges incident at each vertex.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This is a construction for this family; it is not a formalization of Vizing’s theorem for all simple graphs.

Their actual deficiency equals the weighted Petersen mask cut. Every arbitrary whole-clique subset is encoded by a ten-bit mask with matching membership and parity.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This component handles sets containing each clique wholly or not at all. Partially intersected cliques are handled by the family_no_overfull component.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every odd Delta >= 3 and every vertex subset X of the actual sharpness graph, the number of edges internal to X is at most Delta*floor(|X|/2). The proof covers even sets, partially intersected cliques, and whole-clique sets.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The conclusion quantifies over all actual vertex subsets of the constructed family. It does not assert the main theorem for arbitrary graphs.

checked_component_catalog.description: A graph isomorphism preserves edge-colorability, degrees, maximum degree, actual internal-edge counts, and the absence of overfull vertex sets.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: These transport statements allow the explicitly constructed vertex type to be relabelled as Fin n; they are not graph-existence assertions by themselves.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every odd Delta >= 3, there exists a connected simple graph on Fin (4*Delta+5) with maximum degree Delta, no proper Delta-edge-coloring, a proper (Delta+1)-edge-coloring, no Delta-overfull vertex set, and exactly 2*Delta*(Delta+1) edges. The order and edge identities also give |E|=Delta*(|V|-1)/2.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The complete statement of Proposition 7.1. It does not prove the main asymptotic coloring theorem.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every real c < 1/4 and every order bound N, there is a connected simple graph of order n >= N, maximum degree at least c*n, no proper coloring with maxDegree colors, a proper coloring with maxDegree+1 colors, and no maxDegree-overfull vertex set.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The complete statement of Corollary 7.2. The examples approach the quarter coefficient from below and leave the boundary Delta >= n/4 open.

checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Complete Lemma 2.17; no robust partition or coloring theorem is supplied.

checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: A supporting existence result, not the adaptive matching-packing theorem. The general Hall theorem is proved separately in the hall_and_deficiency component.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every positive regular simple graph with no overfull set, the uniform vector belongs to the convex hull of actual perfect-matching indicators. A finite nonnegative probability distribution is constructed with each edge marginal exactly 1/k.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The simple-graph perfect-matching application. The full loopless multigraph matching-polytope theorem and distributions are now proved in separate components.

checked_component_catalog.description: Extracts an edge-minimal noncolorable graph by its actual edge count, removes isolated vertices, proves inheritance of no-overfullness and maximum-degree preservation, and relabels by an actual graph isomorphism to Fin m. The same-maximum-degree extraction explicitly uses Vizing upper bounds.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The structural exclusion of dense critical graphs is not supplied.

checked_component_catalog.description: For finite distributions of actual perfect matchings with exact marginals 1/k, proves failure probability < 1/k for each odd set, at most 10/k for all one-vertex changes of an even set, and at most 11 * ell / k for a family of ell sets. The residual graph, its degree k-1, cut incidences, parity, toggle identities, and all probability bounds are proved.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Complete Lemma 4.7 for finite simple graphs. Prescribing edges while retaining these cut bounds and repeated adaptive matching deletions remain separate arguments.

checked_component_catalog.description: The complete verified Misra-Gries algorithm is transported from its adjacency-list representation to actual finite simple graphs and proper unordered-edge colorings, proving the upper bound Delta(G)+1.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Vizing supplies the maximum-degree preservation in the critical reduction; it does not prove the dense critical exclusion.

checked_component_catalog.description: The host-maximum-degree overfull vertex-set predicate is proved equivalent to existence of an intrinsically overfull mathlib subgraph with exactly the same maximum degree. The induced witness, equality of its maximum degree, actual edge counts, and the converse for arbitrary subgraphs are all proved.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This establishes exact agreement of the formal target with the manuscript obstruction; it does not prove sufficiency for edge coloring.

checked_component_catalog.description: Hall’s equivalence and its deficiency form are proved for actual matching subgraphs, with arbitrary finite side sizes. The deficiency construction uses h dummy vertices and counts the unmatched original vertices.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Complete Theorem 2.3 and Corollary 2.4. No balanced-side hypothesis is imposed.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every finite loopless multigraph, the convex hull of actual matching indicators equals the nonnegative edge weights satisfying the degree and odd-set inequalities. Parallel copies are retained. The degree-inequality polytope is reduced to the proved perfect-matching polytope by a doubled graph; both directions and the matching-indicator correspondence are proved.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Complete Theorem 2.9, not only its perfect-matching application.

checked_component_catalog.description: Every point of the actual multigraph matching polytope has a finite distribution on actual matchings with the prescribed edge-copy marginals. Uniform weights 1/k are feasible under degree at most k and no k-overfull set. Every positive-weight matching covers all degree-k vertices. For a positive regular multigraph the distribution is supported on perfect matchings, with all zero-weight indices removed.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Proves the consequences following Theorem 2.9 for arbitrary loopless multigraphs. It does not prove the later adaptive matching-packing arguments.

checked_component_catalog.description: The robust graph hypotheses produce an explicit simple alternating path avoiding W, with prescribed uncovered endpoints and at most ceil(2/theta)+1 matching edges. Both vertex sequences are injective, actual matching edges are distinct, and each forward graph edge is outside the matching. The matching need not lie in G.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Complete Lemma 2.15. Repeated matching-packing and reserve arguments remain separate.

checked_component_catalog.description: Actual simple robust cores are embedded by endpoint-preserving injective maps into the finite host multigraph edge copies. Under the stated real degree and error bounds, every cut of size at most k+b has total minority shore size at most one. An actual union of whole cores differs in at most one vertex. A uniform order threshold is proved before quantifying graph data.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Complete Lemma 2.18, with real k, a, b and explicit sufficient threshold 3 < nu^2*c^2*n. It does not supply a robust partition.

checked_component_catalog.description: For actual finite bipartite graphs, the crossing-degree assumptions imply the necessary finite-network cut inequalities and yield real edge weights with prescribed row and column sums. The balanced bound is d/lambda. The unequal-side bound is strengthened to 2*theta/(2*c-1), implying the stated 3*theta/(2*c-1). Weights vanish on nonedges and empty sides are included.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Complete Lemmas 5.6 and 5.9. The circulation theorem is proved in included, attributed source; no flow or cut existence is assumed in the graph results.

checked_component_catalog.description: The side-normalized bipartite robust-expansion range shrinks from tau to any positive sigma at most tau, with new parameter min(nu,alpha*sigma/4), under the stated crossing-degree bounds. All incidence estimates use actual graph edges.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Complete neighborhood-expansion conclusion of Lemma 6.4. The usual new-parameter inequality mu <= sigma follows for positive order; the empty-graph branch proves the expansion inequality without claiming this additional parameter admissibility.

checked_component_catalog.description: The three matching-deletion probability bounds are proved also for loopless multigraphs, with all parallel copies counted separately. Deleting a matching is realized as a multigraph on the subtype of remaining edge copies; the residual cut and degree identities are proved. The required perfect-matching distributions are constructed.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Strengthens Lemma 4.7 to the multigraph setting used in the completion arguments. Edge prescriptions and adaptive repeated deletions are not proved here.

checked_component_catalog.description: Every finite loopless bipartite multigraph has a proper k-edge-coloring exactly when all degrees are at most k. Every parallel edge copy receives its own color value. The proof derives no-overfullness by counting the smaller bipartition shore, obtains a matching covering maximum-degree vertices from the proved matching polytope, deletes its actual copies, and inducts on k. The zero-degree case is included.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Complete König edge-coloring input in Section 2.3; no multigraph fan elementarity theorem is supplied.

checked_component_catalog.description: For finite real coordinate spaces and a linear map into a specified subspace, a proved halving correction at every residual gives an exact correction with twice the one-step norm bound. The correction series, continuity, convergence, exactness, and coordinate bounds are proved.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: An internal analytic helper. It does not establish the graph-specific one-step corrections or the manuscript fractional triangle-decomposition lemma by itself.

checked_component_catalog.description: Actual color classes of a proper multigraph edge coloring are edge-copy matchings. Each color contributes at most floor(|X|/2) internal copies, so every k-colored multigraph has at most k*floor(|X|/2) internal edges on each vertex set.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The necessary no-overfull condition for all finite loopless multigraphs. Sufficiency in the bipartite case is proved separately by König’s theorem.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every 0<eta<1/2, the positive threshold eps0=min(eta,1/(32*(2+10/eta))) is chosen before all finite vertex types and actual simple tripartite graphs. Under the exact local-balance, degree, and missing-neighbor hypotheses, actual triangle weights have incidence one on every actual edge and lie in [1/(2k),3/(2k)]. The signed link corrections, residual contraction, uniform-deficit bounds, and convergent correction series are all proved and composed. Empty first and second parts are included with the third part unrestricted.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This is a fractional decomposition of the actual tripartite graph. The finite absorber is proved separately. Approximate integral packing, iterative absorption and the full dense extension remain unproved.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every finite simple graph, a maximum matching leaves exactly the maximum of the untruncated integer differences o(G-X)-|X| vertices uncovered. The odd-component count uses the actual vertex-deleted graph. All integer differences are bounded and an actual vertex set attains equality. A matching attaining the deficiency is constructed by adding universal vertices, applying the proved Tutte theorem, and restricting the perfect matching. Maximum is measured by actual unordered edge counts. The empty graph is included.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Complete Theorem 2.5 for finite simple graphs. The underlying Tutte theorem is a proved declaration in the pinned mathlib dependency, not an assumed formula.

checked_component_catalog.description: Full Lemma 2.10 for actual loopless multigraph edge colorings: all exceptional vertices are covered, both sides have equal color-class coverage, the side sizes differ by at most two between colors, each vertex is covered in exactly its degree many colors, and both footprint bounds hold. The proof constructs actual two-color switches and minimizes two finite potentials.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The initial q-edge-colorability is a hypothesis of the manuscript lemma; existence of that initial coloring in the later applications is a separate obligation.

checked_component_catalog.description: Full Lemma 2.11: color the actual edge copies at the distinguished vertex injectively, then extend greedily under the strict 2s<k bound for all other degrees.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This lemma treats a finite loopless multigraph with at most one high-degree vertex.

checked_component_catalog.description: Full Lemma 2.12, including real q: an actual sparse vertex deletion, the three-vertex edge bounds, and 6q<k give a proper coloring of all edge copies. The proof colors the core and two stars, assigns palettes by Hall, and colors the central parallel copies.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The deletion and degree bounds are properties of actual edge copies, including arbitrary parallel multiplicities.

checked_component_catalog.description: The explicit finite product of Bernoulli masses is normalized, nonnegative for 0<=p<=1, and has the required joint coordinate probabilities. Unused coordinates are marginalized exactly.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The model samples finitely many independent Boolean coordinates with a common probability p.

checked_component_catalog.description: Full Lemma 2.14 for the actual independently sampled subgraph. A failed robust-neighborhood condition yields actual vertex-set witnesses. Their edge-count tails and a union bound give failure probability at most 4^m exp(-p*nu^2*m^2/24), strengthening the manuscript factor 2.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This proves robust expansion for the sample. Simultaneous degree control is proved separately, and the later adaptive packing is not established by the reserve lemma alone.

checked_component_catalog.description: A uniform order threshold, chosen before the vertex types or graph, produces one actual bipartite spanning subgraph contained in G with robust parameter p*nu/2 and all degree deviations from p*Delta strictly below 2*epsilon*m. This proves the reserve-selection step of adaptive packing.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The reserve-selection component of Step 1; it is now assembled into the complete adaptive packing theorem.

checked_component_catalog.description: Full Lemma 5.3: the actual simple part is injected into the multigraph edge copies; its complement retains every other copy. The actual prescribed coloring determines missing-color edges, local balance, exact deficit identities, and an equivalence between full coloring extensions and exact triangle decompositions.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The equivalence does not itself prove that the encoded graph has a triangle decomposition.

checked_component_catalog.description: Every actual locally balanced subgraph of G[U] is enumerated and decomposed into positive simple directed cycles. The tagged finite family covers each remainder exactly, is edge-disjoint within each tag, has all cycle vertices in U, and satisfies sum(3*length)<=|U|^2*2^(|U|^2).
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: This enumerates and counts the cycles; placement and assembly of the absorber in the dense host are separate results.

checked_component_catalog.description: Full Lemma 5.10 for an actual directed graph whose edges advance through six classes. Graph-derived common vertex demands are corrected by the unequal-side flow theorem. The resulting supported edge probabilities lie strictly in (0,1), are exactly balanced at every vertex, and differ from mu by at most c1*mu*theta.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Explicit choices are c1=12/(2c-1) and theta0=min(1/4,1/(4c1)); both depend only on c. This constructs expected balance, not a sampled integral reserve.

checked_component_catalog.description: Full Lemma 5.5: from the actual tripartite density and missing-neighbor bounds, a uniform threshold gives one finite absorber for every locally balanced subgraph of G[U]. Its actual edges avoid G[Z], its vertex support outside U avoids Z, its edge-plus-auxiliary-vertex count is at most 4*h^2*2^(h^2), and both its default decomposition and every activated decomposition consist of actual host triangles. Cycle enumeration, simultaneous disjoint placements and exact edge coverage are all proved. A literal mathlib subgraph adapter proves that its vertex set is exactly its support and that its actual edge and vertex counts are the quantities bounded in the manuscript.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The epsilon restriction is written 16*h*epsilon<=gamma, equivalent to the manuscript for h>0 and meaningful when h=0. This is the bounded finite absorber; approximate integral packing and iterative absorption are still separate obligations.

checked_component_catalog.description: For every prescribed matching in an actual finite simple graph, there is an actual maximum matching covering all vertices covered by the original. The proof switches actual two-color components and maximizes retained coverage secondarily. A greedy matching covers any prescribed set Z whose vertices each have degree greater than 2|Z|; the maximum-matching extension retains this coverage.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: These are matching-selection inputs to Step 2 of adaptive packing. They do not derive the degree inequalities for the actual outside-reserve graph or prove the adaptive matching sequence and load invariant.

checked_component_catalog.description: An actual maximum matching internally supplies a Hall witness. Double-counting actual graph edges proves that its uncovered left-side count is at most (2*a*m+t)/d when both side orders are at most the ambient m, ordinary degrees lie between d-a and d+a+u(v), the load u is nonnegative with total at most t, d>0 and a>=0. Exact matching-edge/covered-vertex identities also prove equal uncovered side counts for balanced graphs.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The degree-based deficiency theorem. The actual outside-reserve graph, its degree identities, matching completion and adaptive invariant are proved by the later packing modules and assembled in Overfull.adaptive_bipartite_packing.

checked_component_catalog.description: From actual degree and total-load bounds, construct an actual globally maximum matching covering the prescribed saturated vertices. The positive-capacity variant derives the saturated vertex set and its size from the load function. The manuscript specialization keeps the ambient m distinct from the reduced side sizes, proves equal uncovered-side counts, and obtains exactly h<=(16+2*c0)*epsilon*m/gamma.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The degree-based matching-selection component. The actual working graph, completion and adaptive induction are now proved and assembled in Overfull.adaptive_bipartite_packing.

checked_component_catalog.description: The finite Bernoulli product law permits a distinct success probability at every coordinate. Its normalization, exact joint probabilities, exact expectation, exponential moment, and both Chernoff tails are proved. An event and expectation transfer theorem covers arbitrary finite outcome spaces satisfying the independent joint law.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Finite joint-law formulation of the independent-indicator part of Lemma 2.2. No Mathlib measure-space interface for infinite underlying outcome spaces is included; every finite independent-indicator law used in the manuscript is represented.

checked_component_catalog.description: Uniform sampling of actual k-element subsets of a finite population. Exact subset counts and complement sampling prove the exponential-moment bounds for both signs. The actual expectation and the two-sided Chernoff constant 1/3 are proved, including the empty population and all degenerate samples.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The actual hypergeometric finite law, not an assumed concentration or moment estimate.

checked_component_catalog.description: Switch an actual matching along one alternating path, or simultaneously along a vertex-disjoint family relative to the original matching. Covered vertices are exactly the old covered set and the path ends. Every reserve edge and its degree contribution are tracked in the original reserve even when paths use only its unused subgraph.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Actual augmentation of supplied paths; construction of the disjoint paths is proved separately and used in the complete packing theorem.

The paths are not assumed. An induction protects the last pair while constructing the preceding paths, then joins that pair outside their union.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The path-family construction used in the full matching-completion and packing theorems.

checked_component_catalog.description: Construct a partner-closed forbidden set, enumerate the actual uncovered pairs, find disjoint short paths and complete the matching. The resulting actual ambient subgraph has vertex set exactly the complement of S, uses no reserve edge at S or the saturated set Z, uses at most one at every vertex, and has total reserve degree at most 2*ell*h.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: A complete local matching-completion theorem; it is assembled with actual residual-graph selection and online induction in Theorem 2.16.

checked_component_catalog.description: Exact degree and reserve-load identities for the actual union of pairwise edge-disjoint matching subgraphs. Working degrees after vertex deletion, equality with the manuscript load counts, exact load increments, integer-capacity preservation, and the unused reserve degree are proved.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: All degrees are degrees of actual graph deletions; none of the required working-degree conclusions is assumed.

checked_component_catalog.description: Identify the deleted graph with the sum of the remaining bipartite sides, preserve degrees and exact uncovered counts, and construct an actual ambient matching outside both the reserve and all old edges. It covers every remaining saturated vertex and satisfies both deficiency bounds using the actual total reserve load.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The complete graph-theoretic Step 2, with the small-constant hypotheses supplied by the parameter lemmas.

checked_component_catalog.description: Solve the exact finite reserve-use recurrence, bound its geometric factor by exp(8*ell/gamma), justify the rounded capacity and saturated-set size, and choose all small constants and order slack before the graph. The permitted round count includes the zero-round case.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Numerical components of Theorem 2.16, combined with the actual graph construction rather than used as substitutes for it.

checked_component_catalog.description: A uniform threshold produces the initial actual reserve with expansion, degree control, minimum degree and integer slack. Subsequent reserve degree loss equals the actual used-edge load; the unused reserve and the entire graph left after all selected matchings retain half its original robust parameter.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: The initial and residual graphs are actual graphs. These results provide the initialization and final expansion assertion of Theorem 2.16.

checked_component_catalog.description: One actual round constructs an ambient matching perfect outside the current forbidden set, disjoint from all old edges, preserving the integer reserve capacity and satisfying the total-load recurrence. Exact Fin.snoc graph and load identities connect the enlarged union to the next finite history.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: No completion or working-graph degree conclusion is assumed by the round theorem.

checked_component_catalog.description: Full Theorem 2.16. The positive error and order threshold are chosen before the graph. One fixed rule, selected before the adversary, constructs actual pairwise edge-disjoint matchings perfect outside the sets presented so far and leaves a bipartite robust (p*nu/4,tau)-expander after every permitted prefix. All reserve choices, path constructions, degree/load accounting, rounded capacities and quantitative induction are proved.
checked_component_catalog.scope_limit: Full Theorem 2.16, with uniform constants and one rule for all admissible adaptive inputs. Direct prescribed-set and perfect-matching corollaries prove robust expansion after removing any subfamily. This does not prove the manuscript main theorem.
